newsitem.title: UK: Europe buys most Iraq crude as SOMO nears target.
newsitem.headline: Europe buys most Iraq crude as SOMO nears target.

text.p: European refiners are set to absorb the lion's share of renewed Iraqi oil sales as Baghdad closed easily this week on 500,000 barrels a day (bpd) of export contracts, oil traders said on Thursday.
Europe is also likely to see shortly the first spot sale of Iraqi crude in six years since U.N. sanctions were imposed for Baghdad's invasion of Kuwait.
Iraq's State Oil Marketing Organisation (SOMO) had by Thursday signed 16 contracts worth a combined 435,000 bpd.
Four more contracts totalling 65,000 bpd, three with Russian firms and one with a European company, were in the pipeline, company officials said. The United Nations has so far approved 13 contracts.

U.S. refiner Coastal Corp and U.S. trading house Bayoil stole the limelight this week with the shipment of a Very Large Crude Carrier (VLCC) each of Basrah Light crude from Iraq's Gulf terminal Mina al-Bakr.
Bayoil's 30,000 bpd looks likely to join Coastal's 60,000 bpd in Coastal's Caribbean Aruba refinery ending up in American cars and heating tanks.
But European firms will dominate liftings in the months to come as Iraq secures the $2 billion worth of sales over six months permitted under the U.N.'s oil for-for-food exchange.
At current market prices SOMO will not need to export more than 500,000 bpd to hit the $2 billion ceiling.
"We calculate that about two-thirds is coming to Europe," said a trader at one company which signed a contract with SOMO this week.
"We've already had indications that Kirkuk will be available (on the spot market)," the trader said.

European firms, including Turkey's Tupras, have already signed up for a combined 250,000 bpd of Iraqi oil. Tupras has already lifted a cargo of Kirkuk from the Turkish end of Iraq's pipeline outlet to the Mediterranean at Ceyhan.

French Total and Elf, Italian Oil Energy, Anglo-Dutch Shell, Austrian OMV, Bulgarian Chimimport and Spanish Repsol all are expected to refine allotments in their own refineries. Italian Agip, expected to sign soon, would also take its share home.
Elf, Repsol and Shell or Trafigura are next in line to lift Kirkuk from Ceyhan, shipbrokers said.

Dutch trader Trafigura is expected to take its crude to eastern Europe. Swiss Taurus looks the most likely candidate to offer a cargo on the spot market in Europe, or possibly into the United States, traders said.

Some of the additional 100,000 bpd allotted to six Russian firms is also expected to end up in European refineries via spot sales, although its not yet clear how the Russian buyers will market their Iraqi supplies.
"I think we'll see the Russians offering some (in Europe) which is ironic because its Russian crude which is suffering the consequences," a trader said.

Although international benchmark Brent has remained firm in the face of Iraqi shipments this week, Russian Urals blend price differentials have taken a big hit this week. Urals sold this week at Brent minus $1.05, down from Brent minus 30 cents.
Japan's Mitsubishi Corp, representing five Japanese refiners, will load later in December from Mina al-Bakr. The 45,000 bpd Japanese purchase represents only 10 percent of Iraq's exports.
